issues.t: Frame rust in salt-belt states
issues.sym: Flaking, scaling or holes in the frame rails, rusted crossmembers, or a shop saying the frame is unsafe or not fit to tow with.
issues.why: Road salt eats into the frame and underbody over time. FJs from snowy, salted-road states are much more likely to have it. Toyota did not run a frame program for the FJ.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift, especially before buying. Rustproofing each year slows it down. Heavy rot needs frame repair by a welding shop or a replacement frame.

issues.t: Inner front fenders crack or bulge
issues.sym: Cracks, tears or bulges in the inner fender sheet metal under the hood, often on both sides. In bad cases the fender shifts and the front doors bind.
issues.why: Owners of early FJs report the inner fender and crumple-zone area stressing and tearing, often after off-road use or rough roads. Owners say later trucks were improved.
issues.next: Open the hood and look along both inner fenders near the firewall and shock towers. Have a body shop assess any cracks; they can be welded and reinforced.

issues.t: Shudder at 35-45 mph
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration like driving over rumble strips at about 35-45 mph under light throttle, often in top gear or on a slight incline.
issues.why: The torque converter lock-up clutch in the automatic can grab unevenly. Owners say it was worst on 2007 trucks. Old or low fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have it changed with Toyota fluid. Some owners avoid it by driving in 4 instead of D. If it keeps happening, a shop may replace the lock-up solenoid or torque converter.

issues.t: Clunk or bump from behind when stopping or starting
issues.sym: A clunk, thunk or a feeling of being bumped from behind just before stopping or when pulling away.
issues.why: The slip joint in the rear driveshaft sticks when its grease dries out. Toyota issued bulletin T-SB-0046-12 for 2007-2013 automatic 4WD FJs with an improved driveshaft.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft slip yoke cleaned and greased; many owners grease it every oil change. If that does not fix it, a dealer can install the updated driveshaft.

issues.t: Front differential grinding or groaning in 2WD
issues.sym: A cyclic grinding or groaning noise from the front while driving in 2WD that goes away when you shift into 4WD.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-SB-0026-15 covers this on 2004-2015 Tacoma, 4Runner and FJ Cruiser. The noise comes from the front differential while it is not driving the wheels.
issues.next: Tell the shop the noise stops in 4WD; that points them to the bulletin. Have the front differential fluid checked too.

issues.t: Head gasket failure
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, occasional misfires, white exhaust smoke, especially at startup, or overheating.
issues.why: The early 4.0L V6 can develop head gasket leaks at higher mileage, letting coolant into the cylinders.
issues.next: Watch coolant level and the temperature gauge. Ask a shop for a cooling system pressure test and a test for exhaust gas in the coolant. Avoid buying one that smokes at startup.

issues.t: Front brake calipers stick and drag
issues.sym: The truck pulls to one side when braking, a hot or burning smell from one wheel, one wheel much hotter than the others, or fast pad wear on one side.
issues.why: The caliper pistons and slide pins corrode and stick, so the pad keeps rubbing on the rotor. It is one of the most reported FJ repairs.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected. A stuck caliper should be replaced along with pads and often the rotor on that side.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing or hub wears out
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and changes when turning, or play in the wheel.
issues.why: Front wheel bearings and hubs wear out, faster with big tires, lifts and off-road use.
issues.next: Have the wheel checked for play and noise. A bad bearing can overheat, so do not put it off for long.

issues.t: Front CV axle boots tear
issues.sym: Grease slung around the inside of the front wheel, a clicking noise when turning, or vibration.
issues.why: The rubber CV boots on the front axles crack with age and suspension travel, letting grease out and dirt in.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot quickly. Once the joint clicks, the whole axle is usually replaced.

issues.t: Front lower ball joints wear out
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The lower ball joints wear with mileage, big tires and off-road use.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked for play. Worn joints should be replaced, since a failed joint can let the wheel collapse.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim, the battery keeps going dead, or a whining noise from the engine.
issues.why: The alternator wears out with age. It is among the more common FJ repairs reported by owners.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested. Replace the alternator if it is not charging, before you get stranded.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed air-fuel sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a code for the bank 1 or bank 2 sensor 1 air-fuel sensor. The truck may run normally or use more fuel.
issues.why: The upstream air-fuel sensors wear out at higher mileage. A failing sensor or misfires can also damage the catalytic converters.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replace the failed sensor; do not ignore a misfire, since it can ruin a converter.

issues.t: Oil consumption at higher mileage
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the low oil light comes on, or blue smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: As the 4.0L V6 ages, it can start using oil. Running it low can lead to engine damage; some owners report needing a replacement engine.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and top it up. Keep up with oil changes. If use climbs quickly, have a compression and leak-down test done.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch at high mileage
issues.sym: A rattle or slap from the front of the engine, mostly at cold start, or a check engine light for cam and crank timing.
issues.why: The 4.0L V6 uses a timing chain. At high mileage the chain, tensioner and guides can wear, especially with poor oil change habits.
issues.next: Have the noise diagnosed. Keeping oil clean and full helps the chain last. A worn chain is replaced with its tensioner and guides.

issues.t: Blend door actuator clicking
issues.sym: A clicking or tapping noise behind the dash, or air temperature that will not change properly.
issues.why: A small motor that moves the heater blend door fails or strips its gears.
issues.next: Have the HVAC system checked. The actuator is a small part but can take some dash work to reach.

issues.t: Left foot rest comes loose or falls off
issues.sym: The dead pedal (left foot rest) feels loose or falls off the floor.
issues.why: Owners widely report the foot rest mounting coming loose on FJs.
issues.next: Re-secure it or replace the foot rest so it cannot slide under the pedals.

issues.t: Rear swing door hinge area cracks
issues.sym: Creaking from the rear door, the spare tire wobbling, or cracks around the rear door hinges.
issues.why: The heavy spare tire hangs on the rear swing door, and the weight can stress the hinge area over time, worse off-road or with bigger tires.
issues.next: Inspect around the hinges when buying. Do not mount a much larger spare without a separate carrier. Have a body shop repair cracks early.

issues.t: Water leak at the rear access doors
issues.sym: Water on the rear floor or seats after rain or a car wash, near the small rear-hinged access doors.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletin 00707 for water leaking past the access door seals.
issues.next: Have a dealer or body shop do a water test and reseal or adjust the doors per the bulletin.

issues.t: Fluid leak from the dash-top gauge pod
issues.sym: Liquid seeping from or a bubble inside the three-gauge pod on top of the dashboard (compass, temperature, inclinometer).
issues.why: Toyota bulletin SB-0026-11 covers fluid leaking from the accessory meter on 2007-2009 FJ Cruisers.
issues.next: Have a dealer replace the gauge pod under the bulletin. Wipe up any fluid so it does not damage the dash.

issues.t: Hard start or rough idle after the battery is disconnected
issues.sym: After a battery change or jump start the engine is hard to start or idles low and rough; sometimes a crankshaft sensor code (P0335) sets.
issues.why: The engine computer loses its learned idle settings when power is cut, and low battery voltage can set false sensor codes. Toyota has bulletins for both.
issues.next: Let it idle and drive normally to relearn, or have a shop run the idle relearn. Test the battery if codes keep coming back.

issues.t: Clutch pedal slow to return in freezing weather
issues.sym: On manual-transmission FJs, the clutch pedal comes back up slowly in sub-freezing temperatures.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin SB-0129-10 covers slow clutch pedal return in the cold on these trucks.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the clutch hydraulics against the bulletin. Bleeding the system or replacing a part usually fixes it.

issues.t: Creak or tick from the windshield or rear glass
issues.sym: A creak, tick or rattle from the top or bottom of the windshield or the top of the rear glass, often over bumps.
issues.why: Toyota bulletin T-SB-0141-10 traces this to the bonded glass stoppers.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or glass shop to service the stoppers per the bulletin.

issues.t: Musty A/C smell or water on the floor
issues.sym: A musty or sour smell from the vents, or water on the front passenger floor.
issues.why: The A/C drain tube can clog with debris or insect nests, so water backs up in the evaporator case. Toyota has bulletins on blocked drains and HVAC odors.
issues.next: Have the A/C drain cleared and the evaporator cleaned. Replace the cabin air filter if fitted.

issues.t: Rear access door panel can crack and loosen seat belt (recall)
issues.sym: Cracks in the inner panel of the rear access doors, or a front seat belt that feels loose at its anchor.
issues.why: Repeated hard closing of the rear access doors can crack the panel that holds the front seat belt retractor, which could come loose in a crash. Recall 13V-098.
issues.next: Close the access doors gently. Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN and inspect the panels; the repair is free.

issues.t: Add-on seat heaters can short and burn the seat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the seat, a seat heater that stops working, or scorch marks on the seat.
issues.why: Dealer-installed accessory seat heaters can have their wiring damaged when the cushion is compressed, causing a short and fire risk. Recalls 14V-743 and 16V-396.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater. A Toyota dealer will disconnect it and refund the accessory cost.

issues.t: Accessory driving lights are too bright (recall)
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash you when the factory accessory driving lights are on.
issues.why: Accessory auxiliary lamp kits used 55-watt bulbs that are brighter than federal rules allow. Recall 13V-163 swaps in 35-watt bulbs.
issues.next: If your FJ has the accessory driving lamps, have a Toyota dealer check your VIN for the free bulb swap.

issues.t: TRD brake kit wheel weights can damage a brake line (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leaking at a front wheel, a soft pedal, or the brake warning light, on trucks with the TRD big brake kit.
issues.why: On FJs with the TRD brake kit, wheel balance weights in the wrong spot can rub a front brake tube and cause a leak. Recall 12E-046.
issues.next: If you have a TRD brake kit, have a dealer check your VIN and the brake lines. Do not drive with a soft pedal.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: The low tire pressure light does not come on even when a tire is low.
issues.why: The tire pressure monitoring system was not calibrated correctly on some trucks. Recalls 11V-148 and 11V-185.
issues.next: Check tire pressures with a gauge monthly. Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN and recalibrate the system free.

issues.t: Tire label may show wrong spare tire info (recall)
issues.sym: The tire placard on the door jamb lists the wrong spare tire size or pressure, mostly on trucks with accessory wheels.
issues.why: Some FJs with accessory wheels and tires got a placard that did not match the spare. Recall 14V-475.
issues.next: Check that your spare matches the placard. A Toyota dealer will apply a corrected label free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor may be miscalibrated (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag off light behaves oddly, or the airbag may not turn on for an adult passenger.
issues.why: The passenger seat occupant sensor could be thrown out of calibration after some accessory installs. Recall 13V-014.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN and recalibrate the sensor for free.

issues.t: Load capacity label may be wrong (recall)
issues.sym: The door-jamb load label lists a weight limit that is not correct.
issues.why: Some trucks got inaccurate load labels, which could lead to overloading and tire failure. Recall 13V-123.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN for a corrected label.

issues.t: Steering shaft weld may fail (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering, or in the worst case the steering wheel stops turning the wheels.
issues.why: On FJs built August 7-20, 2013, the intermediate steering shaft may have a weak weld. Recall 15V-081.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN right away. They replace the shaft for free.

issues.t: Ball joint bolts may be loose on Trail Teams Ultimate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front suspension or wandering steering on a Trail Teams Ultimate Edition.
issues.why: After shock and spring work on these trucks, the front lower ball joint and arm bolts may not have been tightened enough and could fall out. Recall 14V-539.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN and torque the bolts for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, will not start, or stalls while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can fail. Recall 20V-012 covers many Toyota models including some 2014 FJ Cruisers.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN. The fuel pump is replaced free.

issues.t: Dealer-installed accessories may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Running boards or other dealer-installed accessories rattle or feel loose.
issues.why: Fasteners on accessories installed by the regional distributor may not have been tightened enough. Recall 14V-828.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN and tighten the bolts.
